dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Coloring
dossier_meta.statement_text: Question Are there any (0,2)-graphs with chromatic number exactly three?
dossier_meta.context_text: A (0,2)-graph is a graph such that every pair of distinct vertices has either 0 or 2 common neighbours. It is fairly easy to see that a (0,2)-graph is necessarily regular and a variety of other properties can be shown to hold. Although (0,2)-graphs with chromatic number 2, 4 and 5 are known it is open as to whether there can be any (0,2)-graphs with chromatic number exactly three.
dossier_meta.references_text: - *[P] Payan, Charles: On the chromatic number of cube-like graphs, Discrete Math. 103 (1992), no. 3, 271--277.
